title: Switch generated API-reference evidence from JSON to Markdown for both TS and Rust extractors
objective: Owner-directed follow-up to G-DOCS-API-AUTODISCOVERY-AND-NOISE-FILTER. Owner asked directly whether an LLM handles JSON and Markdown the same way; honest answer: not quite -- for the one real consumer that exists today (an agent reading the whole file), Markdown's lower punctuation overhead and header-based structure is a genuinely better fit than JSON's, and this repo already has a proven precedent for exactly this rendering shape (libs/graph/core/tests/snapshots/public-api.txt: `### signature` header + doc body). The earlier 'stay JSON' recommendation over-weighted a Graph IR ingestion pipeline that does not exist yet; that migration, if it happens, reprocesses from Rust/TS source again regardless of this file's current format, so nothing is lost by switching now. Scope: re-render docs/generated/api/rust/*.json and docs/generated/api/ts/*.api.json as *.md using the same `### signature` + doc-body shape, keeping the noise filter and auto-discovery from the prior two tasks unchanged.
validations: Verified TypeDoc's actual reflection API before writing a custom renderer (not assumed): read SignatureReflection.d.ts, DeclarationReflection.d.ts, Reflection.d.ts, Comment.d.ts, types.d.ts from the installed 0.28.20 package, then a live probe script confirmed Type.toString(), SignatureReflection.parameters/type, and Comment.summary[].text all behave as expected against a real target (packages/ui) before committing to the approach; probe script deleted after use.
Rust side (tools/rust-api-docgen): cargo build -p grafting-rust-api-docgen compiles clean after switching serde_json::json! output to hand-rendered `### signature` + doc-body text.

TS side (generate-api-docs.mjs): direct read of the real generated ui.api.md confirmed clean, correct output (interfaces/properties/functions/type aliases all render with correct types and docs, matching the source).

Found and fixed a real quality problem in the TS 'application' (multi-file) mode before shipping: file-based module reflections were named after their full relative path, so every descendant's qualified name repeated e.g. 'apps/architecture-studio/src/canvas-composition' in full. Fixed via pathSegmentName (basename only) plus treating undocumented module wrappers as transparent grouping nodes (no entry of their own, but children still walked) -- verified by regenerating architecture-studio.api.md and reading the real before/after.

Real drift proof repeated on both sides with the new Markdown format (not assumed to still work after the rewrite): hand-corrupted docs/generated/api/ts/ui.api.md and separately docs/generated/api/rust/grafting-compute-cpu.md -- both --check runs failed naming the correct file, both passed clean after regenerating.
pnpm run docs:check: full 7-step chain passes end to end.
cargo check --locked --workspace: clean after the tools/rust-api-docgen rewrite.

git status / find docs/generated/api -type f: old *.api.json (ts) and *.json (rust) files removed, not left alongside the new *.md files -- exactly 10 files total, same as before, only extension and content changed.

Size comparison across all 6 real Rust crates: 2.4 MB (raw rustdoc JSON) -> 234 KB (curated JSON) -> 160 KB (curated + noise-filtered JSON) -> 154 KB (curated + filtered Markdown) -- final format is not meaningfully smaller in bytes than the prior JSON step, but is the one the owner's own stated reasoning (today's only real consumer is an agent reading the whole file, not a program) favors.
artifacts: tools/scripts/README.md (both extractor sections and the rust-api-docgen section rewritten for the Markdown format and the reasoning behind it)
risks: Rust side is low risk: the public-api crate's own Display already renders a clean signature string (proven by the existing public-api.txt snapshot); this task only changes serialization from a JSON map to `### sig` + body text, same underlying data.

TS side is the real risk: TypeDoc's Node API has no built-in 'render this reflection as a short text signature' helper the way Rust's public-api crate does. Verifying TypeDoc's actual Signature/Type reflection API (toString support, comment.summary shape) against its real .d.ts before writing a custom renderer, rather than assuming an API surface.
Old .api.json files are being replaced by .api.md/.json(rust) equivalents; the old filenames are removed, not left stale alongside the new ones, to avoid two competing artifacts for the same data.
